newsitem.title: UK: Air Foyle reconsiders Boeing 747-200 freighter plan.
newsitem.headline: Air Foyle reconsiders Boeing 747-200 freighter plan.

text.p: Independent British carrier Air Foyle is considering reactivating a plan to lease a Boeing 747-200F and operate scheduled international freighter services, said chairman Chris Foyle.

He told Reuters in an interview that he had found a suitable aircraft that would be available "on terms satisfactory to us" with the aim of operating from London to a European point and on the the Middle East and Far East.
Adding a transatlantic Britain-United States sector was also a possibility, he said.

"The idea would be to sell space to two or three principal customers, which we have identified. If the project goes ahead -- and this is not yet certain -- we would start between March and October next year," he added.
Foyle said that Air Foyle had first looked at entering the 747F operating market four years ago when, among other potential customers, he had held talks with Virgin Atlantic Cargo.
"At the time, 747-200 freighters -- we are only interested in -200s (not the earlier generation, less powerful -100s) -- were fairly easy to come by," said Foyle.
"But at the time, we were not properly set up to enter the 747F market and when our circumstances were right, the situation had changed," he said.
He recalled that by then, carriers such as Southern Air Transport and Atlas Air had purchased most available 747-200Fs and passenger 747-200s which they converted into freighters.
"Then in 1996 when we were again looking at a 747F project, rates softened throughout the marketplace. Our timing was wrong...we were overtaken by events," he said.
Air Foyle currently concentrates on managing and operating aircraft on behalf of owners, which include TNT and Antonov Design Bureau.
